I'm building a comprehensive list of "guardrails" (safety, security, development process, and delivery/CI-CD controls) in a Salesforce PWA Kit repo (zimmermann-pwa) for the user. I already have full context on AGENTS.md and .claude/rules/*.md (branch rules, Tier 1/2 file protections, coding workflow, accessibility/a11y ast-grep rules, payment-credential-logging rule, dangerouslySetInnerHTML/XSS rule). I need you to survey the remaining pieces I haven't read yet and report back what guardrails/gates they implement. Specifically read and summarize:

1. `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml` — what does the `tier1-guard` job actually check and warn about?
2. `.github/workflows/qa.yml` — what CI gates run on PRs (unit tests, storybook, playwright, lighthouse, etc.), and any branch-scoping logic (e.g. BrowserStack per-story scoping, change-scoped E2E).
3. `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml` — what does the SIT gate check, and on which branches.
4. `.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml`, `deploy-sit.yml`, `deploy-uat.yml`, `deploy-stg.yml`, `deploy-prod.yml` — briefly, what approval gates or environment protections exist for each deploy target (just skim for `environment:`, required reviewers, manual approval triggers — don't need full YAML detail).
5. `.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml` and `.github/workflows/weekly-agents.yml` — what do these automate (one line each).
6. `semgrep.yml` at repo root — what security rules does it define (e.g. payment-credential-logging, XSS/dangerouslySetInnerHTML) — list the rule ids/descriptions.
7. `coderabbit.yaml` at repo root — what does it configure (AI PR review scope, tier-1 detection, commit format enforcement).
8. `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/*.yml` (there are img-missing-alt.yml, icon-button-missing-aria-label.yml, clickable-non-interactive-element.yml) — confirm these are accessibility lint rules, one line each on what they catch.
9. `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` and `scripts/hooks/commit-msg` — what do these git hooks enforce (e.g. Contentful drift check, blocking edits to derived AI config files, conventional commit format, secret scanning).
10. `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md` — summarize the supervised-edit rules for release/hotfix branches (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, fix/release-* sub-branch flow, GitFlow back-merge rules).
11. `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md` — what's the policy for bumping the upstream @salesforce/retail-react-app dependency.
12. Check `.env.sample`'s header comment for how env var scoping (shared/tier/personal/auto) and secret handling works.

Report back as a structured list grouped by category (CI/CD delivery gates, security scanning, git hooks, accessibility enforcement, release process, dependency policy). Keep it factual and concise — under 600 words. Cite file paths for each item.

66	          # the latest SHA's checks, and a "skipped" job counts as passing
67	          # (see the always()/skipped handling on e2e-localhost below) — so
68	          # skipping here just means nothing e2e/storybook-relevant changed

106	      # Resolve e2e_scope to either "full" or a single area name (e.g.

125	          # Narrow to "checkout" only if every e2e-relevant changed file is

127	          # shared/global path, or one no area has claimed) falls back to

140	      # or branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app uses to link a

145	      # only runs when at least one key is found, scoped to that story's

2	
3	# Opens a GitHub issue when @salesforce/retail-react-app ships a new release.
4	# This is an automated notifier — not a drift detector. See .docs/upstream-policy.md
5	# for what to do with the issue (usually: skim release notes, close, update
6	# .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md).
7	
8	on:
9	  schedule:
10	    - cron: '0 0 * * 1'  # Every Monday at midnight UTC
11	  workflow_dispatch:      # Allow manual trigger for testing
12	
13	permissions:
14	  issues: write
15	  contents: read
16	
17	jobs:
18	  check-upstream-release:
19	    name: Check for new PWA Kit upstream release
20	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
21	
22	    steps:
23	      - name: Checkout
24	        uses: actions/checkout@v4
25	
26	      - name: Fetch latest upstream release tag
27	        id: upstream
28	        run: |
29	          RESPONSE=$(curl -sf \
30	            -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
31	            -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \
32	            https://api.github.com/repos/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/releases/latest)
33	          LATEST_TAG=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.tag_name')
34	          RELEASE_URL=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.html_url')
35	          PUBLISHED_AT=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.published_at' | cut -c1-10)
36	          echo "tag=$LATEST_TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
37	          echo "url=$RELEASE_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
38	          echo "published=$PUBLISHED_AT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
39	
40	      - name: Read baseline tag from upstreamBaseline.md
41	        id: baseline
42	        run: |
43	          BASELINE_TAG=$(grep -oP '(?<=<!-- upstream-release-tag: )[^\s]+(?= -->)' .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md || echo "UNSET")
44	          echo "tag=$BASELINE_TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
45	
46	      - name: Check for existing open issue for this release
47	        id: existing
48	        env:
49	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
50	        run: |
51	          COUNT=$(gh issue list \
52	            --label "upstream-sync" \
53	            --state open \
54	            --json title \
55	            --jq '.[].title' \
56	            | grep -c "${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}" || true)
57	          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
58	
59	      - name: Open tracking issue
60	        if: |
61	          steps.upstream.outputs.tag != steps.baseline.outputs.tag &&
62	          steps.existing.outputs.count == '0'
63	        env:
64	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
65	        run: |
66	          LATEST_TAG="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}"
67	          RELEASE_URL="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.url }}"
68	          PUBLISHED="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.published }}"
69	          BASELINE_TAG="${{ steps.baseline.outputs.tag }}"
70	
71	          gh issue create \
72	            --title "Upstream release available: $LATEST_TAG" \
73	            --label "upstream-sync,needs-review" \
74	            --body "$(cat <<EOF
75	          ## New Salesforce PWA Kit release detected
76	
77	          | | |
78	          |---|---|
79	          | New upstream release | [$LATEST_TAG]($RELEASE_URL) |
80	          | Published | $PUBLISHED |
81	          | Current baseline | $BASELINE_TAG |
82	
83	          ---
84	
85	          ## What to do
86	
87	          Our policy is **bump opportunistically, not on a schedule.** See [.docs/upstream-policy.md](../blob/main/.docs/upstream-policy.md).
88	
89	          1. Open the [release notes]($RELEASE_URL).
90	          2. Skim for:
91	             - **Security** — CVE fixes, dependency patches we are exposed to.
92	             - **SDK** — changes in \`pwa-kit-runtime\`, \`pwa-kit-react-sdk\`, \`commerce-sdk-react\`, or \`pwa-kit-dev\` that affect code we use.
93	             - **Bug fixes or features** we have been waiting for.
94	          3. **If nothing relevant:** close this issue with a one-line reason, and update \`Reviewed up to\` in [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../blob/main/.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md). Do not bump.
95	          4. **If something relevant:** bump \`@salesforce/retail-react-app\` (and any related SDK packages), run \`npx tsc --noEmit\`, \`npm run build\`, \`npm run test\`, then update **both** \`Current\` and \`Reviewed up to\` (and the \`<!-- upstream-release-tag: ... -->\` marker) in upstreamBaseline.md.
96	
97	          ---
98	
99	          _Opened automatically by the upstream-release-watch workflow._
100	          EOF
101	          )"
102	
103	      - name: Log no-op reason
104	        if: |
105	          steps.upstream.outputs.tag == steps.baseline.outputs.tag ||
106	          steps.existing.outputs.count != '0'
107	        run: |
108	          if [ "${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}" = "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.tag }}" ]; then
109	            echo "No new release. Latest upstream (${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}) matches current baseline."
110	          else
111	            echo "Issue already exists for ${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}. No duplicate created."
112	          fi

1	# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json
2	# .coderabbit.yaml — Zimmermann PWA Kit
3	# CodeRabbit configuration for AI-assisted PR review
4	# Docs: https://docs.coderabbit.ai/configuration
5	#
6	# Paths target this slim overrides project: `overrides/app/...` (not the upstream monorepo
7	# `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...`). Hooks under `overrides/` are `.ts` per the
8	# TypeScript-only rule.
9	#
10	# NOTE: `version: "2"` and a top-level `custom_instructions:` block previously lived here.
11	# Neither key exists in the current schema (schema.v2.json) — confirmed by validating
12	# against the published schema and cross-checking real production configs (appsmith,
13	# bruno, MONAI), none of which use either key. custom_instructions's 12 rules have been
14	# migrated to the path_instructions entry below so they actually take effect.
15	
16	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	# LANGUAGE & TONE
18	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	language: "en-US"
20	
21	reviews:
22	  # Post a high-level summary on every PR
23	  high_level_summary: true
24	
25	  # Post a poem... no. We're engineers.
26	  poem: false
27	
28	  # Collapse walkthrough for smaller PRs to reduce noise
29	  collapse_walkthrough: false
30	
31	  # Request changes (not just comment) when critical issues found
32	  request_changes_workflow: true
33	
34	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
35	  # PROFILE — sets the overall review strictness
36	  # "assertive" = CodeRabbit will push back harder on issues
37	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
38	  profile: "assertive"
39	
40	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	  # PATH FILTERS — excludes mechanically-generated/derived files from
42	  # review scope entirely (distinct from path_instructions above, which
43	  # only changes review *criteria*, not whether a file is reviewed at
44	  # all). These files are regenerated from other source files already
45	  # covered by path_instructions/code_guidelines below — reviewing the
46	  # derived copy too is redundant, and scripts/hooks/pre-commit already
47	  # blocks hand-editing them directly, so review findings on them can't
48	  # be actioned there anyway. Excluding lock files per CodeRabbit's own
49	  # recommendation (docs.coderabbit.ai/guides/review-instructions).
50	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	  path_filters:
52	    - "!package-lock.json"
53	    # Generated by scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs from .claude/rules/*.md + AGENTS.md
54	    - "!.cursor/rules/**"
55	    - "!.vscode/instructions/**"
56	    - "!.github/copilot-instructions.md"
57	    # Generated by scripts/generateRegistry.mjs from overrides/app/
58	    - "!.claude/registry/*.md"
59	
60	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
61	  # PATH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS
62	  # This is the most powerful CodeRabbit feature for this project.
63	  # Different review instructions per file path.
64	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
65	  path_instructions:
66	    # ── Repo-wide baseline (was a non-functional top-level `custom_instructions:`
67	    #    key — migrated here since path_instructions is the mechanism that
68	    #    actually exists in the schema; matching entries apply cumulatively
69	    #    alongside the more specific ones below) ─────────────
70	    - path: "overrides/**"
71	      instructions: |
72	        This is a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
73	        This is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 (not a fork).
74	        The stack is React 18, Chakra UI v2, React Query v4, React Hook Form v7, and Express SSR
75	        on Salesforce Managed Runtime.
76	
77	        For every PR, check:
78	
79	        1. TYPESCRIPT-ONLY INSIDE overrides/ — Every file created or modified under `overrides/`
80	           must use `.ts` or `.tsx`. Flag any `.js`/`.jsx` introduced inside `overrides/`.
81	
82	        2. SSR SAFETY — Any hook or component that accesses window, document, localStorage, or
83	           sessionStorage must have a typeof window !== 'undefined' guard. SSR failures cause
84	           complete page breakdowns.
85	
86	        3. REACT QUERY CACHE — Any mutation that changes basket, customer, or order state must
87	           call queryClient.invalidateQueries() with the correct query key. Missing invalidations
88	           cause stale data that persists until page reload.
89	
90	        4. CHAKRA THEME USAGE — No inline style values for colours, spacing, or typography.
91	           All values must reference theme tokens (e.g. "brand.primary" not "#1A1A1A").
92	           Hard-coded values bypass the design system and break brand consistency.
93	
94	        5. LOCALE AWARENESS — No hardcoded strings in JSX. All user-facing copy must use
95	           react-intl's useIntl() hook and a message ID. Zimmermann serves 18 locales across
96	           6 regions.
97	
98	        6. MULTI-REGION SAFETY — No hardcoded currency symbols, country codes, or locale strings.
99	           Zimmermann serves AU, US, UK, EU, ME, HK (7–8 SFCC sites — US split is TBC).
100	           Use useMultiSite() for site context.
101	
102	        7. EINSTEIN & DATACLOUD EVENTS — Any user interaction that qualifies as a commerce event
103	           (view product, add to cart, begin checkout, click recommendation) must fire the
104	           corresponding Einstein and DataCloud event. Missing events corrupt analytics and
105	           personalisation data.
106	
107	        8. ACCESSIBILITY — Target WCAG 2.2 AA. All interactive elements must have accessible
108	           labels. Images must have alt text. Focus management must be correct in modals and
109	           drawers.
110	
111	        9. PERFORMANCE — Mobile page speed is a top priority. Flag any new synchronous blocking
112	           operations in the SSR render path. Flag any new third-party scripts loaded without
113	           async/defer. Flag images rendered at full resolution where a thumbnail size is used.
114	
115	        10. NO CONSOLE LOGS IN PRODUCTION CODE — Debug logs must be removed before merge.
116	            Sensitive data (tokens, customer PII, basket contents) must never be logged.
117	
118	        11. CLAUDE CODE PROVENANCE — If a PR description or commit message indicates Claude Code CLI
119	            was used to generate the changes, apply heightened scrutiny to shared hooks and
120	            components. Verify the scope of changes matches what was described in the PR.
121	
122	        12. CONVENTIONAL COMMITS — Every commit message in this PR must follow the format:
123	            type(scope): description
124	            Valid types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync
125	            Scope is optional but encouraged (e.g. product-tile, checkout, global-e, contentful).
126	            If any commit does not follow this format (excluding Merge and Revert commits), flag it
127	            and request it be amended before merge. A non-compliant commit message will produce an
128	            incorrect or unclassifiable changelog entry.
129	
130	    # ── Tier 1: Design tokens ───────────────────────────────
131	    - path: "overrides/app/theme/foundation/**"
132	      instructions: |
133	        TIER 1 — DESIGN SYSTEM FROZEN FILE.
134	        This file contains Zimmermann brand design tokens. Treat every change with maximum scrutiny.
135	
136	        Check for:
137	        - Any colour value changes — flag the old and new hex values explicitly
138	        - Any font size, weight, or family changes — flag what changed
139	        - Any spacing scale changes — note which scale values were modified
140	        - Any breakpoint value changes — these affect every responsive component
141	        - Whether the change is additive (new token) or destructive (modifying existing token)
142	
143	        Destructive changes to existing tokens will affect every component in the design system.
144	        Always flag: "This change modifies an existing design token. Confirm with UI Designer that
145	        all consumers have been audited."

150	        TIER 1 — HIGHEST RISK HOOK. useCurrentBasket is consumed by cart, checkout,
151	        order summary, promo code, and bonus product components simultaneously.
152	
153	        Every change requires:
154	        - Explicit audit of all import consumers: grep -r "use-current-basket" overrides/
155	        - Confirmation that the return shape has not changed

184	        Check for:
185	        - Any hardcoded locale or currency values
186	        - Changes to site alias resolution logic
187	        - Whether changes have been tested against all configured locales, not just en-AU

191	      instructions: |
192	        TIER 1 — RUNTIME CONFIGURATION. These files control feature flags, API endpoints,
193	        and proxy routing for all environments.

195	        Check for:
196	        - Any hardcoded API keys, secrets, or credentials — immediate block, must be in env vars

218	        - Any change to the deploy or activate steps — flag what changes and why

227	        Check for:

234	    - path: "overrides/app/components/header/**"

236	        TIER 2 — GLOBAL HEADER. This renders on every page. Review as if this is production-critical.

239	        - Any change to the navigation data structure consumed from useNavigation
240	        - Any new prop added to a child component — confirm it's optional with a sensible default
241	        - Mobile/desktop breakpoint logic — confirm both viewports are covered
242	        - Accessibility: keyboard navigation, focus management, aria labels on interactive elements
243	        - Any new external script or asset load — this adds to page weight on every route

275	        Check for:
276	        - Correct handling of all price types: regular, sale/strikethrough, promotional, range
277	        - Currency formatting — confirm it uses the locale-aware formatter, not hardcoded symbols

281	    - path: "overrides/app/pages/checkout/**"
282	      instructions: |
283	        SQUAD A — CHECKOUT. This is the highest-revenue-risk area of the codebase.

1	#!/bin/bash
2	# Pre-commit hook:
3	#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
4	#   2. If any Studio Experiences component (experiences/*.tsx) is staged,
5	#      regenerate definitions.ts and stage it automatically.
6	#   3. Protect derived configuration files from direct edits.
7	#   4. Block .env.sample commits that contain secret-class key values.
8	#
9	# Setup: hooks are managed by Husky v9 — run `npm install` and they are installed automatically.
10	#   Husky sets core.hooksPath to .husky/_ and .husky/pre-commit calls this script.
11	#   If you ever need to install manually (e.g. npm install --ignore-scripts):
12	#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
13	#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
14	
15	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	# 0. Ensure node is on PATH.
17	#    Git hooks run in a non-interactive shell — version managers (nvm, fnm,
18	#    volta) are not sourced automatically. Try each in turn; fail loudly if
19	#    node still can't be found so the developer knows what to fix.
20	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	
22	if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
23	  # nvm (most common on macOS)
24	  export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
25	  [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"
26	
27	  # fnm
28	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null && command -v fnm &>/dev/null; then
29	    eval "$(fnm env 2>/dev/null || true)"
30	  fi
31	
32	  # volta
33	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
34	    export PATH="$HOME/.volta/bin:$PATH"
35	  fi
36	
37	  if ! command -v node &>/dev/null; then
38	    echo "  ❌  pre-commit: node not found. Make sure your version manager is"
39	    echo "      initialised (nvm, fnm, or volta) and node is installed."
40	    exit 1
41	  fi
42	fi
43	
44	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	# 1. Registry regeneration — runs on every commit to keep .claude/registry/
46	#    in sync. Stages any updated registry files automatically.
47	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
48	
49	staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
50	
51	registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
52	registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
53	registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
54	registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
55	registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)
56	
57	if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
58	  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
59	  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
60	  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
61	  git add .claude/registry/
62	fi
63	
64	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
65	# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
66	#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
67	#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
68	#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70	
71	if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
72	  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
73	    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
74	    || true)
75	
76	  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
77	    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
78	    node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null
79	    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
80	  fi
81	fi
82	
83	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
84	# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
85	#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
86	#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
87	#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
88	#     automatically.
89	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
90	
91	skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
92	  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
93	  || true)
94	
95	if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
96	  echo ""
97	  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
98	  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'
99	
100	  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
101	    echo ""
102	    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
103	    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
104	  fi
105	
106	  echo ""
107	  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
108	  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
109	  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
110	  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
111	  echo ""
112	fi
113	
114	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
115	# 2. Contentful Studio Experiences codegen
116	#    When any experiences/*.tsx file is staged, regenerate definitions.ts
117	#    and stage it automatically. Blocks the commit on codegen failure.
118	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
119	
120	experiences_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
121	  | grep -E 'overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/.*\.tsx$' \
122	  || true)
123	
124	if [ -n "$experiences_staged" ]; then
125	  echo "Studio Experiences component staged — regenerating definitions.ts..."
126	
127	  REAL_EXPERIENCES="overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences"
128	  tmp_exp=$(mktemp -d)
129	  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_exp"' EXIT
130	
131	  # Populate temp dir with the staged version of each .tsx.
132	  # Files that are not staged are copied from the working tree so the generator
133	  # sees a complete set. definitions.ts is excluded — it is the output target.
134	  for f in "$REAL_EXPERIENCES"/*.tsx; do
135	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
136	    name=$(basename "$f")
137	    [[ "$name" == "definitions.ts" ]] && continue
138	    if echo "$experiences_staged" | grep -qF "$f"; then
139	      git show ":0:$f" > "$tmp_exp/$name"
140	    else
141	      cp "$f" "$tmp_exp/$name"
142	    fi
143	  done
144	
145	  if ! CF_EXPERIENCES_DIR="$tmp_exp" node scripts/contentful/generateDefinitions.mjs; then
146	    echo ""
147	    echo "  ❌  Contentful codegen failed. Fix the errors above and try again."
148	    exit 1
149	  fi
150	
151	  cp "$tmp_exp/definitions.ts" "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
152	  git add "$REAL_EXPERIENCES/definitions.ts"
153	  echo "  ✓  definitions.ts updated and staged."
154	fi
155	
156	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
157	# 3. Derived configuration file guard
158	#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
159	#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
160	#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
161	#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
162	#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
163	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
164	
165	blocked_files=()
166	
167	# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
168	modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)
169	
170	while IFS= read -r file; do
171	  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue
172	
173	  # Only check files in derived locations
174	  case "$file" in
175	    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
176	    *) continue ;;
177	  esac
178	
179	  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
180	  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
181	  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
182	  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue
183	
184	  # Extract all source paths from the synced-from comment
185	  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2, ...] — ... -->
186	  synced_sources=$(echo "$synced_line" \
187	    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
188	    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//')
189	
190	  [[ -z "$synced_sources" ]] && continue
191	
192	  # If ANY source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
193	  # update — the developer edited a .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
194	  # Skip it.
195	  staged_names=$(git diff --cached --name-only)
196	  any_source_staged=false
197	  while IFS= read -r src; do
198	    src=$(echo "$src" | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//;s/[[:space:]]*$//')
199	    [[ -z "$src" ]] && continue
200	    if echo "$staged_names" | grep -qxF -- "$src"; then
201	      any_source_staged=true
202	      break
203	    fi
204	  done <<< "$(echo "$synced_sources" | tr ',' '\n')"
205	  if $any_source_staged; then
206	    continue
207	  fi
208	
209	  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
210	  blocked_files+=("$file")
211	
212	done <<< "$modified_staged"
213	
214	if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
215	  echo ""
216	  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
217	  echo ""
218	  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
219	    echo "       $bf"
220	  done
221	  echo ""
222	  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
223	  echo ""
224	  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
225	  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
226	  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
227	  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
228	  echo ""
229	  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
230	  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
231	  echo ""
232	  exit 1
233	fi
234	
235	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
236	# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
237	#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
238	#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
239	#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
240	#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
241	#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
242	#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
243	#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
244	#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
245	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
246	
247	if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
248	  secret_violations=()
249	
250	  while IFS= read -r line; do
251	    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
252	    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
253	    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
254	    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
255	    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
256	    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue
257	
258	    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
259	    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
260	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
261	      continue
262	    fi
263	
264	    # Value looks like a JWT
265	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
266	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
267	      continue
268	    fi
269	
270	    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
271	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
272	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
273	      continue
274	    fi
275	
276	    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
277	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
278	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
279	      continue
280	    fi
281	
282	    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
283	    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
284	      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
285	      continue
286	    fi
287	
288	  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)
289	
290	  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
291	    echo ""
292	    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
293	    echo ""
294	    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
295	      echo "    $v"
296	    done
297	    echo ""
298	    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
299	    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
300	    echo ""
301	    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
302	    echo ""
303	    exit 1
304	  fi
305	fi
306	
307	exit 0

2	# commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
3	#
4	# Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
5	#          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
6	
7	commit_msg=$(cat "$1")
8	
9	# Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
10	if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
11	  exit 0
12	fi
13	
14	# Conventional commits pattern
15	# type(optional-scope): description
16	# upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
17	pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'
18	
19	if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
20	  echo ""
21	  echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
22	  echo ""
23	  echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
24	  echo ""
25	  echo "  Types:"
26	  echo "    feat           new feature"
27	  echo "    fix            bug fix"
28	  echo "    docs           documentation only"
29	  echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
30	  echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
31	  echo "    perf           performance improvement"
32	  echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
33	  echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
34	  echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
35	  echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
36	  echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
37	  echo ""
38	  echo "  Scope examples (optional but encouraged):"
39	  echo "    product-tile  checkout  auth  header  search"
40	  echo "    global-e  adyen  contentful  searchspring"
41	  echo "    pwa-kit-runtime  commerce-sdk-react"
42	  echo ""
43	  echo "  Examples:"
44	  echo "    feat(product-tile): add sale badge for discounted variants"
45	  echo "    fix(checkout): resolve shipping method not persisting on refresh"
46	  echo "    upstream-sync(pwa-kit-runtime): apply v3.18.0 SSR cache fix"
47	  echo "    chore(deps): update @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react to 5.3.0"
48	  echo "    test(use-current-basket): add guest basket merge coverage"

1	# Release & Hotfix Branch Rules
2	
3	**Read this file in full before taking any action when `git branch --show-current` matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`.** These rules apply *in addition to* the Hard Rules in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). On `feature/*` and `fix/*` branches they do not apply and this file can be ignored.
4	
5	See the branch table in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules for which branch merges where.
6	
7	## Back-merge rules (GitFlow)
8	
9	To prevent `develop` drifting from production:
10	- When a `release/*` branch is merged to `main` at go-live, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
11	- When a `hotfix/*` is merged to `main`, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
12	- When a `fix/release-*` is merged into its `release/*` parent and the release later ships, the forward-merge to `develop` happens as part of the release back-merge above — no separate action.
13	
14	## Release Branch Behaviour
15	
16	When on a `release/*` branch, the following rules apply in addition to all Hard Rules.
17	
18	**Before writing any code, always:**
19	1. State a plan — which files will change, what will change in each, and why.
20	2. Assess blast radius — how many components, hooks, or pages consume each file being changed? Flag explicitly if any file has more than 3 consumers or is Tier 2 or above.
21	3. Wait for explicit developer confirmation before making any edit, including trivial ones.
22	
23	**Allowed on release branches:**
24	- Read-only skills: `/generate-changelog`, `/pr-checklist`, `/code-quality`
25	- Trivial non-code changes (copy corrections, version bumps, feature flag toggles) — plan + confirm required
26	- Code logic fixes — only on a `fix/release-{version}_{description}` sub-branch, never directly on the release branch
27	
28	**Not allowed on release branches:**
29	- New features or scope additions not in the release
30	- Refactoring
31	- Dependency changes
32	- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches
33	
34	**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**
35	
36	The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.
37	
38	```bash
39	# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
40	git checkout release/v0.1.0
41	git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description
42	
43	# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
44	gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
45	```
46	The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (when CI lands). See [architecture.md > Environments](architecture.md) for the full six-tier environment topology (Local · Dev · SIT · Stage · UAT · Prod).
47

1	# Upstream update policy
2	
3	How we handle new releases of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` (and the surrounding PWA Kit SDKs).
4	
5	## Principle
6	
7	**Bump opportunistically — not on a schedule.** Stay on the current version unless a release contains something we actually care about.
8	
9	Reasons to bump:
10	- **Security** — CVE fix, dependency patch with a known vulnerability, advisory we are exposed to.
11	- **SDK** — a change in `pwa-kit-runtime`, `pwa-kit-react-sdk`, `commerce-sdk-react`, or `pwa-kit-dev` that affects code we depend on (SSR, routing, hooks we use, build pipeline).
12	- **Bug fix or feature we have been waiting for** — a fix to behaviour we currently work around, or a feature that lets us delete custom code, or will help us on implementing a planned feature.
13	
14	Reasons **not** to bump:
15	- A release with only template/UI changes that we have already overridden.
16	- A release whose changelog touches packages or paths we do not use.
17	- "It's been a while."
18	
19	## Discipline
20	
21	When the upstream-release-watch workflow opens a tracking issue (see [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml)):
22	
23	1. Open the linked release notes.
24	2. Skim for the three categories above.
25	3. If nothing relevant, close the issue with a one-line reason and update `Reviewed up to` in [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](memory/upstreamBaseline.md). **Do not bump.**
26	4. If something relevant, bump — then update `Current` and `Reviewed up to` together.
27	
28	## What we do not do
29	
30	- **No drift detection script.** We do not diff our `overrides/` against the upstream template on a schedule. Drift is the *point* of the overrides pattern.
31	- **No two-track review.** There is no separate "SDK package review" vs "template code skim." If we bump, we bump; the changelog tells us what to test.
32	- **No bump because it's been N weeks.** Time alone is not a reason.
33	
34	## Related
35	
36	- Current baseline: [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](memory/upstreamBaseline.md)
37	- Watch workflow: [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml)
38	- CI security gate (once CI lands): `npm audit --audit-level=high` — fail on new highs only.

# ── Environment switching ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This file is the documented template for every variable the project uses. Each
# active line below is preceded by its own `# scope:shared`, `# scope:tier`,
# `# scope:personal`, or `# scope:auto` comment line (parsed by
# scripts/switchEnv.mjs, ignored by everything else — kept on its own line,
# not trailing on the KEY=value line, so a blank placeholder here still reads
# as genuinely empty to the pre-commit secret guard):
#   scope:shared   — same value across all 6 tiers (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod)
#                    AND same for the whole team. Lives in .env.shared; included
#                    in `push`/`init`'s pull to/from GitHub Environments.
#   scope:tier     — differs per tier. Lives in the gitignored .env.<tier> for
#                    whichever tier you're pointing local dev at; also
#                    included in `push`/pull.
#   scope:personal — tier-independent like shared, but a PERSONAL credential
